column2: “The victim is Tetsuo Igarashi, forty-two.{r}{p}President of a company that develops and sells computer software.”

“The crime came to light on Monday.{r}{p}He was always supposed to be at work by eleven. When he hadn't shown up by past noon and wasn't answering his phone, one of his employees went to his apartment.{r}{p}The door was naturally locked
so he couldn't get in.{r}{p}He was about to head back, but apparently thought he'd peek in through the window.”

“The apartment is on the first floor, and you can get around to the inner garden just by climbing a simple fence.{r}{p}There the employee spotted the president through the window, lying in the living room in his pajamas.”
“The window was locked too, so he waited for the police, had the manager open the door, and when they went in,
Igarashi had been strangled with his own necktie.”
“Nothing that grand.{r}{p}The killer probably killed Igarashi, then used his key to lock the door and left.{r}{p}That's all there is to it.”
Sunday, between about nine in the morning and noon.”
“Let me explain the relationships around the victim.”
“Igarashi used to be a programmer at another company, but about three years ago he went independent and founded his current one.{r}{p}What was it called...
or whatever, and apparently that was a huge hit.”
This is why old guys are trouble.
“A browser, you mean.{r}{p}Software for viewing web pages on the Internet.”
That brow-ser.{r}{p}It was a huge hit and the company grew fast.{r}{p}But there were plenty of problems, too.”
“First, a former colleague from the old company, Satoshi Nakajima, sued, claiming Igarashi's software was made by plagiarizing much of his own programs.”
“The trial is still ongoing, but neither side shows any sign of giving an inch, and it's become a quagmire.”
“What complicates things further is Megumi Imamura, who was Nakajima's fiancée.”
“Right.{r}{p}Apparently Igarashi had been hitting on her for a long time.{r}{p}Knowing she was engaged.{r}{p}And on top of that, Igarashi has a wife and child.”
“Megumi reportedly wouldn't give him the time of day, but the moment Igarashi made it big, things seem to have changed.”
“Put simply, yes.{r}{p}She secretly started seeing Igarashi.”
“But before long, Nakajima noticed something odd about her, pressed her, and everything came out. The engagement was broken off.”
“Meaning she'd have married him if it hadn't come out?{r}{P}”
But it didn't go that smoothly.{r}{p}On top of that, Igarashi seems to have lost interest in Megumi as if his earlier obsession had been a lie.”
“So she was dumped by both of them.”
“Exactly.{r}{p}Over this affair, both Nakajima and Megumi undoubtedly resented Igarashi deeply.{r}{p}And of course his wife,

Tokuko, too.{r}{p}When she learned of the mistress, she even wounded Igarashi swinging a kitchen knife.{r}{p}Fortunately the injury was minor and the police weren't called, but she's been living at her parents' with their daughter ever since.”
“Normally a woman resents the other woman, though.”
In that sense, Tokuko may be the masculine type.{r}{p}Talking with her, I didn't sense anything like anger toward Megumi.”
So those three had motives to kill Igarashi.”
a former employee of Igarashi's company.”
“Did he steal programs from him this time?{r}{P}”
Cash.{r}{p}Embezzlement, in other words.{r}{p}He was caught, fired, and his wife lost patience with him, so now he lives alone.”
“Guys like that always want to pin the blame on others.”
“Nozaki repeatedly phoned Igarashi with threats, even saying 'I'll kill you.'”
“These four are the prime suspects.{r}{p}Every one is suspicious, but there's no decisive proof.”
“What were the suspects' alibis for that time?{r}{P}”
“It'd be quicker if you read their statements.{r}{p}I've got them here, typed up.”
The Lieutenant handed over four files, a few stapled pages each.
If you notice anything, would you tell me?{r}{P}”

“Yeah.{r}{p}All you can tell from this is the killer...
The two of them stared at me in shock.
“You really know who the killer is?{r}{P}{p}Who is it?{r}{P}”
I let them wait a moment before speaking.
“Check them one by one and it's easy, isn't it?”
“Check them one by one and it's easy, isn't it?”
“Check them one by one and it's easy, isn't it?”
“The necktie used as the weapon arrived at ten, so the crime was committed after that.{r}{p}So Nakajima's alibi holds.”

“The necktie used as the weapon arrived at ten, so the crime was committed after that.{r}{p}It would have been impossible for Megumi to commit the crime and reach the department store by ten-thirty.{r}{p}So her alibi holds.”
“Tokuko had an injured hand.{r}{p}It's hard enough for a woman to strangle a man, and with an injured hand she'd never choose a necktie as the weapon.”
